Development of this hub involves the installation of storage tanks and liquefaction equipment at Port Tampa Bay. As proposed, T-RICH will provide an intermediate storage hub for captured CO accessible to emitters anywhere in the State of Florida via all transport modes including 2 existing rail, truck, pipeline, and ship infrastructure systems into the hub site at Port Tampa Bay. This project’s main objective was to determine that the development of T-RICH is technologically feasible and commercially viable. Existing transport infrastructure at Port Tampa Bay and the vicinity includes interstate highways, major state roads, existing pipeline rights of way upon which new CO pipelines could 2 be built, the CSX rail network, and shipping channels with deep water access. The study determined the technical, physical, and regulatory requirements for the installation of CO storage tanks, gas conditioning 2 and transfer equipment, and extensions of nearby existing roads, rail lines and pipelines into the site. The study evaluated the siting, design, and technical requirements for a minimum storage capacity of 30,000 metric tons (mt) which would support processing up to 2,000,000 mt of CO captured in Florida annually 2 for permanent sequestration or EOR use. The plan includes the ability to expand the capacity of the T- RICH site as more CO is captured by emitters in the region and the State, and more marine vessels would 2 be built in the U.S. and added to transport the additional quantity of captured CO delivered to and stored 2 at the hub site for subsequent shipping to the northern Gulf Coast.
